codeReview.title: Code Review
codeReview.description:
Leave inline comments on your teammates' code and exchange feedback.

Reviewing with context on which line and what intent code was written for

lifts both code quality and the whole team's skill together.

recruitment.title: Team Recruiting
recruitment.description:
Find teammates that fit your project based on tech stack and interests.

Post whether you need a backend developer or a designer,

and student developers with similar goals will apply.

portfolio.title: Portfolio

Completed projects are automatically organized into your own portfolio.

Easily build and share a development history that shows

what tech you used and what role you played at a glance.

NO_README.label: No README
NO_README.guide: Add an overview, how to run it, and the tech stack so visitors can understand the project.

NO_DESCRIPTION.label: No description or topics
NO_DESCRIPTION.guide: Add a one-line description and topics in the repo's About section.

NO_HOMEPAGE.label: No deploy link
NO_HOMEPAGE.guide: If it's deployed, add the URL to Website in About — a live demo stands out.

NO_TESTS.label: No tests
NO_TESTS.guide: No test folder found. Start by testing one core feature.

TOO_FEW_COMMITS.label: Too few commits
TOO_FEW_COMMITS.guide: Two commits or fewer. If it's practice, consider making it private or archiving it.

WEAK_COMMIT_MESSAGES.label: Weak commit messages
WEAK_COMMIT_MESSAGES.guide: Most recent commits say little ("update", "fix"). Describe what changed and why.

FORK_HEAVY.label: Mostly forks
FORK_HEAVY.guide: Under 30% of your repos are your own. Try starting a small personal project.

NO_PROFILE_README.label: No profile README
NO_PROFILE_README.guide: A README in the repo named after your username shows on your GitHub profile.
